newsitem.title: UK: UK's FTSE opens one percent lower after Dow plunge.
newsitem.headline: UK's FTSE opens one percent lower after Dow plunge.

text.p: UK shares opened sharply lower on Friday in response to fears of an early hike in U.S. interest rates which wiped over two percent off the Dow overnight.
The FTSE 100 index of leading shares was 32.7 points lower at 4,364.8 by 0849 GMT. The Dow had finished with a 160-point loss, after being down 63 points at the London close on Thursday.
But dealers said activity was likely to be subdued ahead of the weekend and key U.S. economic data scheduled for later today was also likely to cap London's losses.

"I don't think it will be as exciting as some people believe," said one trader. "I see us wobbling a bit, but the wheels won't be coming off."
"We are not going to match this fall point for point," said another.

Sentiment in the U.S. was hit on Thursday by news of a surge in retail spending at the beginning of this year which was followed by hints that the Federal Reserve may raise U.S. interest rates as early as March 25.
U.S. bonds subsequently tumbled, taking stocks sharply lower.
